description: Why `node:*` is permanently floored, in the shape that makes it so. Node's builtins are ambient `declare module` blocks inside `@types/node`, and the walk that assigns keys starts at a package's entry points — so the module name is not an npm package the project holds, and the package that declares it publishes nothing to walk. Both spellings of the key fail, and differently, and `check` is where a reader who tried them learns that rather than guessing at a third. A package with no subpaths at all says so, because an empty list rendered as nothing reads as the report failing to print one.

names: nothing of `widget` is in this project
It publishes no subpaths at all, so no key in this grammar reaches it.
2 entries checked. 1 reaches nothing; 1 names a package this project does not hold.
